dedupe_keys.name: uscg navigation center gps problem reports and guide tool

description: The US Coast Guard Navigation Center, the civil point of contact for GPS users, collects reports from the public of problems with GPS reception and publishes them through its GPS User Issue Detection and Evaluation (GUIDE) tool and problem report status page. Anyone in any sector, such as mariners, pilots, drivers, surveyors, farmers or operators of timing equipment, can report a disruption through an online form or by telephone, 24 hours a day. Each published report carries a sequential number, the date of the disruption, its location, the user type (marine, aviation, automobile, surveying, timing, transportation, communications, agriculture, research or other), a description with the user's account and NAVCEN's response, the cause found, such as interference, equipment or unknown, and the date the case was closed. The tool shows the last 30 days by default on a map, with longer periods selectable, and entries seen reach from 2022 to 2026. NAVCEN also publishes planned GPS service interruptions, such as military tests, and US Maritime Administration advisories on interference hot spots. Coverage: worldwide reports, mostly from US users. Format and access: web table and map, free; no bulk download seen. Caveats: voluntary reports that NAVCEN states do not verify any degradation of the GPS constellation; many interference events go unreported. Simulation uses: catalogues of GNSS disruption events by sector and place, calibration of interference scenarios and exposure of maritime and aviation navigation. Related records: GPSJam shows interference from aircraft data, and the FAA WAAS reports give measured performance.
